text: At 3:40 in the morning, Taeo still hadn't answered Nib. Selling him would pay every bill. That was what made the offer so hard to refuse.

He sat with his family photograph, then touched the faded patch on his backpack. He used to believe he would always do the right thing. Across the room, Nib watched from beneath his blanket, wide awake.
By morning, Nib had put his knife back in its sheath. Taeo had already accepted Dr. Pyo's invitation to a café. He had answered the message the very minute it arrived.
Taeo told Nib he didn't have to come. Nib was already at the door. As he saw it, Pyo was buying him. He intended to be there.
They reached the tower by Hapjeong Station just before their appointment. Nib got through the revolving door without trouble. The sleepless Taeo went around twice and bumped into the doorman.
Pyo greeted them warmly, with two coffees and a glass of juice waiting. Taeo apologised for the door. Nib checked the room's exits and immediately claimed Pyo's seat against the wall.
Pyo gave it up, only to discover Nib wasn't going to sit. He wanted the view of the entrance. When Pyo offered the juice, Nib said, 'You first.'
Pyo obligingly took a sip. Nib pushed the glass back anyway. Taeo whispered that it cost 13,500 won. Nib's solution was simple: Pyo could drink the rest.

Then Pyo opened his folio. Nobody like Nib had entered an assessment office in twenty years, he said. At Kanghan Institute, Nib would have his own rooms, a garden, a doctor, and people paid to listen.
What caught Nib's attention was the suggestion that Kanghan might send him home. He asked whether Pyo could actually do it. Pyo admitted nobody could yet. Nib told him, 'Then don't say perhaps.'
Pyo turned to Taeo. Surely those conditions were better than an eighteen square metre flat. Taeo couldn't honestly deny it. He admitted Nib would live better there, and Nib heard every word.

As Pyo slid over a tablet, he mentioned that Kanghan had studied arrivals before. Taeo asked about those other arrivals. Pyo's eyes paused before his easy smile returned. Arrival was an old category, he said, and Kanghan was an old institute.

The agreement offered Taeo fifty million won for five years of exclusive observation, with Nib living at Kanghan. Taeo asked where Nib signed. There was no place for him. Pyo said Taeo would sign instead.
Taeo looked up at Nib. Nib looked straight back and gave him no answer. This decision was Taeo's to make.
Taeo set down the pen and pushed the tablet back. His voice stayed quiet, without an apology. 'He's not mine to sell.' Beside him, Nib's folded arms began to loosen.
Pyo accepted the refusal calmly. The review was in twenty-three days, he reminded them. If the panel classified Nib as a construct, Kanghan wouldn't need Taeo's signature.
He left his business card and told Taeo to keep thinking. Taeo stared at it after he left, aware that he had just turned down the price of five thousand lunches.
Nib finally drained the abandoned juice. He explained that it was already paid for. Even after that conversation, there was no reason to waste it.
Outside, they ran into Bae Jungho, the courier Taeo knew from the mart. Bae was directing his stone golem through a service door with three blue crates of bottled juice.
From his height, Nib could see something the others couldn't: the bottom crate was splitting underneath. A bottle was already pushing through. He warned Bae.
Bae shouted for the golem to stop. It obeyed instantly, and the sudden halt tipped the load forward. The crate burst open. Nib darted underneath before Taeo could reach it.

Nib braced the broken base with both hands while the bottles tilted overhead. Bae's panicked instructions only made matters worse. Eventually, Taeo and Bae lowered the crate together, letting Nib pull his hands clear. Every bottle stayed upright.
Bae asked how Nib had spotted the crack. Nib explained that he could see the bottom. Only then did Bae register that the goblin had answered him. Taeo confirmed, wearily, that yes, he talked.
Bae thought Nib would make a good spotter. Nib corrected him: he was a scout, which was better. Then a loan reminder on Bae's wrist wiped away his grin.
Bae owed 640,000 won a month for the golem, with six more years to pay. Broken bottles would have cost him a week's wages. He had taken a draw loan hoping for a rare summon. He had got the golem.
Nib faced the silent construct for a moment. Then Bae hurried back to his delivery, already late, with the golem following his command.
On the river path, Taeo finally apologised for considering the sale. Nib kept walking. Taeo had thought about selling him, he acknowledged. Today, Taeo had said no.
Taeo managed a tired smile and apologised again. Nib informed him that made five apologies for the day. He had been counting.

That night, Taeo ate in the stockroom while the construct stocker worked behind him. Chae finally answered his question: Pyo's warning was true. A construct ruling could take the decision out of Taeo's hands.
To argue that Nib was a person, they needed to show he could choose his work and find someone to vouch for him. Chae arranged a meeting with Ryu Minho at the West practice yard the next morning.
Taeo told Nib through the shared wall, adding that he didn't have to go. In the next room, Nib lifted his hand and pressed it against the wall.
An amber pulse lit Taeo's open palm. The link reached through the wall because Nib had chosen to let him feel it. Taeo had left Nib unanswered all night. Now Nib had answered him.
